name: EDISON INTERNATIONAL
domainRelevance: Edison International operates Southern California Edison, the largest electric utility in California serving 15 million people across 50,000 square miles. The company manages a $40B rate base with 2023 capital expenditures exceeding $5B focused on wildfire mitigation and transmission upgrades. Its exposure to CPUC rate cases and renewable procurement targets positions it as an anchor regulated utility in the western energy transition.
portalRelevance: As an anchor-tier regulated utility in the energy domain, Edison International supplies critical grid stability data and rate-base growth signals for macro-financial models. Its 10-K wildfire liability disclosures and triennial GRC filings provide high-frequency regulatory event hooks that differentiate it from merchant generation peers. The entity serves as a structural benchmark for California-specific energy policy impacts on utility cost of capital.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: quarterly GRC filings with CPUC
10-K wildfire liability updates
monthly SCE load and renewable procurement data
FERC transmission rate filings

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: rate base trajectory versus authorized ROE
wildfire mitigation spend versus CPUC targets
debt-to-capital ratio under CPUC equity requirements

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: pattern match to prior California utility rate case outcomes
comparison of wildfire reserve adequacy versus PG&E
renewable integration cost escalation versus 2020 baseline

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: CPUC general rate case advocacy for 2025-2027 period
wildfire fund contribution hedging via insurance structures
equity issuance pacing to maintain 52% equity ratio

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: board approval of $7B 2024-2026 capex plan
dividend growth alignment with authorized ROE
green bond issuance for transmission projects

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: post-GRC decision stock reaction analysis
SCE customer rate impact versus affordability metrics
FERC ROE incentive award realization

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: recalibration of wildfire probability inputs in cost models
update of renewable procurement sensitivity to IRA credits
adjustment of equity issuance schedule to CPUC equity ratio rulings

functionalNetwork.model: Edison International functions as a regulated network operator whose capital allocation, regulatory filings, and grid investments create measurable state transitions in California energy infrastructure.

suppliers.name: General Electric Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: GE supplied 12 combustion turbines for Mountainview Generating Station expansion completed in 2005; 2022 service contract covers 1.2 GW of SCE peaker capacity under 10-K disclosed maintenance program.

suppliers.name: Siemens Energy AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Siemens delivered 500 kV transformers for SCE's Tehachapi Renewable Transmission Project phases completed 2013-2016; $180M contract disclosed in 2014 10-K capital additions.

suppliers.name: First Solar Inc
suppliers.relationshipNote: First Solar supplied 250 MW of CdTe modules for SCE's Desert Sunlight project online 2014; 2021 PPA amendment added 100 MW under 10-K renewable procurement schedule.

suppliers.name: Sempra LNG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sempra supplies 40 Bcf natural gas annually to SCE's four gas-fired plants under 2020-2025 contracts representing 8% of SCE fuel costs per 10-K Item 1A.

suppliers.name: NextEra Energy Resources LLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: NextEra provides 1,200 MW wind and solar under 2018-2023 PPAs; 2023 capacity factor averaged 32% contributing 4% of SCE retail sales per annual filing.

logisticsPartners.name: Pacific Gas and Electric Company
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: PG&E and SCE jointly operate 500 kV Path 15 and Path 26 corridors under 2002 CAISO agreement; 2023 wheeling volumes exceeded 12 TWh per FERC Form 1 data.

logisticsPartners.name: CAISO
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: CAISO manages SCE's 25,000 miles of transmission under 2020 tariff; SCE paid $420M in 2023 transmission access charges disclosed in 10-K.

customers.name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
customers.relationshipNote: LADWP purchases 800 GWh annually from SCE under 2015 interconnection agreement; 2023 revenue contribution reached $95M per SCE wholesale filings.

customers.name: California Department of General Services
customers.relationshipNote: State of California facilities consumed 1.1 TWh from SCE in 2022 under master service agreement representing 2.5% of SCE retail load per CPUC data.

competitors.name: PG&E Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: PG&E serves 5.5 million electric customers versus SCE's 5 million; both face identical 2023 CPUC wildfire mitigation plan reviews with $2.5B combined spend.

competitors.name: Sempra
competitors.relationshipNote: Sempra's San Diego Gas & Electric operates adjacent to SCE with 2023 rate base of $12B versus SCE's $40B; both compete for CPUC-authorized ROE of 10.3%.

regulators.name: California Public Utilities Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: CPUC authorized SCE's 2021 GRC with $5.5B capital budget and 10.3% ROE; 2025 test year filing submitted July 2024 covers $7.2B spend.

regulators.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FERC approved SCE's 2023 transmission formula rate with $1.8B rate base; incentive ROE adder of 50 bps granted for 2022 Tehachapi upgrade.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC reviews EIX 10-K wildfire disclosures; 2022 settlement of $17M FCPA matter with Edison Mission Energy predecessor entity closed 2018.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte has served as EIX independent auditor since 2004; 2023 audit fee totaled $8.2M per DEF14A with no restatements since 2018.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BofA acted as lead underwriter for EIX $1.25B 4.7% senior notes due 2033 issued March 2023; also provides $1.5B revolving credit facility maturing 2027.

capitalProviders.name: The Vanguard Group
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard holds 11.8% of EIX shares outstanding as of Q3 2024 13F filing; largest institutional holder supporting 3.2% dividend yield.

executiveTeam.name: Pedro J. Pizarro
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Pizarro has served as EIX President and CEO since 2016; 2023 total compensation $14.2M per DEF14A with 62% performance-based equity.

executiveTeam.name: Maria Rigatti
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Rigatti has been EIX Executive VP and CFO since 2016; oversaw $2.1B 2023 equity issuance program disclosed in 10-K.

marketSignals.name: SCE Rate Base Growth Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: SCE rate base grew 7.8% CAGR 2019-2023 reaching $40.1B; 2025 GRC projects 8.5% annual growth through 2027 per CPUC filing.
